permit.general_static_call_theorem: TokenKit.staticcall_kept (TokenKit/Evm/StaticCall.lean, new): for EthLib's real runner, Paris to before Glamsterdam, from a frame at any STATICCALL, with NO assumption on the callee: the run errors, or goes on with a flag 0 or 1, every address reading as before (storage included), same logs, accountsToDelete and refund counter. Proved in general (also through nested calls: processMessage_quiet_static); the KeepsOn-style fallback was not needed.
permit.permit_vrs_0xd505accf: ok_permit_full: every successful run ends by (a) ecrecover = owner, exact gas, recovered word is EthLib's own Ecrecover.compute (recoveredWord), nothing assumed about it; or (b) ERC-1271 (PermitByContract): owner has code, and the answer `out` is the output of the STATICCALL the code makes to the owner (OwnerCall, Sky/OwnerCall.lean): a message `msg` is run by EthLib's runner (Ran (processRunner fork bound) caller msg child, child.error = none, child.output = out) with msg.currentTarget and msg.target = the owner, msg.caller = the token, msg.data = erc1271Input digest r s vw (selector 0x1626ba7e, the digest, offset 64, length 65, r, s, the first byte of the v word, 31 zero bytes: 196 bytes), value 0, isStatic, depth + 1, same block and transaction environment, code = the code of the owner (or of its EIP-7702 delegate, `Routes`), gas = the 63/64 rule of EthLib (messageCallGas) on the gas that the bytes leave at the GAS opcode; out has 32 bytes and its word is the magic value 0x1626ba7e. No assumption on the owner's code. Gas after the call is an inequality. Both routes: nonce slot + 1, allowance slot = value, every other slot kept, exactly one Approval log (permit_readable), invariant kept (supply_permit). The weak form of before the ten-token audit (flag and answer with no call) is kept as PermitKept / PermitEndKept and follows (PermitByContract.kept, PermitEnd.kept); the invariant and readable theorems use it. permit_no_code_fails: wrong signature and an owner without code always reverts.
permit.permit_bytes_0x9fd5a6cf: EVERY SIGNATURE LENGTH. ok_permitBytes_full (no hypothesis on the signature): a successful run passed PermitBytesChecks, was not static, and (a) the length word is 65 and it ended as PermitBytes65AfterEc says (ok_permitBytes65_full: ECRECOVER with exact gas, or ERC-1271 with r, s, v), or (b) the length word is not 65 and it ended as PermitBytesByContract says (ok_permitBytes_other): no ECRECOVER; the owner has code; the code made the STATICCALL that OwnerCall describes, to the owner, static, value 0, with msg.data = erc1271Bytes digest sigBytes (selector 0x1626ba7e, the digest, offset 64, the length L, the L bytes of the signature as the call data gives them, zero bytes up to the next multiple of 32: 100 + ceil32(L) bytes), gas = the 63/64 rule on the gas that the bytes leave at the GAS opcode (exact: 711 decoder + copyCost c + 60 checks + permitCost1 (bodyCostC c or bodyCostD c) + access cost of the owner + 16 + encCost F c + 2, c = L rounded up to 32, F = c + 482 on chain 1 and c + 802 else); the answer has 32 bytes and its word is the magic value; then nonce + 1 and allowance = value were written and one Approval log made (PermitWrites, gas after the call an inequality). L is any length the decoder lets through: 0, below 65, above 65, up to 2^64 - 1 (the decoder reverts above; the checks are conclusions, not hypotheses; any offset word). On top: permitBytes_end, permitBytes_readable, supply_permitBytes, PermitBytesCall, CallsAny, inv_callsAny, process_step_any (every message to the code, no hypothesis on selector or signature), process_step_any_inv, callsAny_process, permitBytes_other_no_code_fails. The 65 theorems are kept as the special case (names with 65, hypothesis hlen).

Assumed, NOT proved, and it cannot be proved in Lean: most of its facts say that one given slot is the balance slot keccak(a, 2) of no address word a (2^160 values of the real, computable keccak). Sequence theorems (inv_calls, inv_callsP, inv_calls65, inv_callsAny; kept as the older, weaker per-message model): a step is a successful top-level call to the token or a change that keeps the storage of the token, and the second kind is ASSUMED (Untouched). The transaction theorems of Sky/Tx.lean (the ten-token audit SKY-3, closed in the fix round of the ONDO audit) do not have this assumption; use them. The base case of the old model: Instance.inv_of_zero and Instance.callsAny_from_zero.

Transaction theorems (supply_transaction, supply_any_transactions, supply_from_zero), run-local hypothesis Seq.TxClean.call / .create with Q := QMsg, part 1: every message m that really enters the code at C during this transaction (re-entry from inside the ERC-1271 STATICCALL to the owner included) satisfies Sep (callKeys m) (keccak separation for its address words, NOT proved). Nothing is assumed about messages outside the run, about the code of the owner contract that permit asks, or about any other code. supply_message_any_depth assumes the same as Seq.Clean of its run.

Transaction theorems (supply_transaction, supply_any_transactions, supply_from_zero), Seq.TxClean.call / .create with Q := QMsg, part 2 (NoDelegation1, used by realFrameKeeps / frameKeepsR for the two permit selectors 0xd505accf and 0x9fd5a6cf only, and from Pectra only): in the state that the frame of each such message starts from, the account at address 1 (the precompile ECRECOVER) holds no EIP-7702 delegation code. A fact of the state, NOT proved and not shown to be kept from one entry to the next: it is assumed at each entry into the token during the run. For permit(bytes) it is carried for every length (the length is not known when the hypothesis is taken), although only a length word of 65 reaches ECRECOVER.

Transaction theorems (supply_transaction, supply_any_transactions, supply_from_zero), Seq.TxClean.create: every code that a creation of this transaction really deposits, when it has the keccak hash of the code of SKY, is that code (no keccak collision on these codes, NOT proved).

Transaction theorems, Seq.TxClean.auths: no EIP-7702 authorization of the transaction sets a code (0 or 23 bytes) with the keccak hash of the code of SKY. Only a keccak collision breaks it; NOT proved.
Transaction theorems, Seq.TxClean.data: the call data of a transaction sent to C is below 2^256 bytes.

Transaction theorems, fork range: each transaction has Fork.dencun <= fork < Fork.glamsterdam (supply_transaction, the cons of Seq.Chain). supply_message_any_depth, realFrameKeeps and frameKeepsR: Fork.paris <= fork < Fork.glamsterdam.

Transaction theorems, start state: Seq.Good C CODE (Inv C) on the block state before the first transaction: C holds the code of SKY (its code hash is keccak256 of the code and not the empty hash) and the invariant holds (supply_any_transactions, supply_transaction); supply_from_zero assumes Seq.HoldsCode and all-zero storage of C instead.

Transaction theorems, supply_message_any_depth only: Seq.Sane C CODE message (if the top message runs at C, it is a call that runs the code of SKY with call data below 2^256 bytes). The transaction theorems prove this from HoldsCode.

Frame rule (Sky/FrameRule.lean frameKeepsR_of_real): no hypothesis. RealFrameKeeps is the form of a frame theorem about EthLib's real runner that uses no fact about the messages the frame sends; supply_permit and supply_permitBytes have that form because TokenKit.staticcall_kept bounds the STATICCALL to the owner (any code) with the real runner.
Instance.KeyFacts (Sky/Instance.lean): the 5 keccak facts left of Sep for the one concrete call m0. NOT proved (each is over 2^160 address words). Only Instance.supply_m0 takes it.
not_covered: permit(bytes) 0x9fd5a6cf with a signature length other than 65 is now proved (ok_permitBytes_other, the ten-token audit SKY-2). What is left on that route: the gas after the STATICCALL is an inequality (the gas the code of the owner uses is not known); no concrete successful-run witness (as for the other permit paths, SKY-5); the 65-byte ERC-1271 call data is stated as erc1271Input and not also as erc1271Bytes; the body costs are stated with the memory sizes as the segments give them (bodyCostC, bodyCostD, encCost, copyCost: differences of memoryGasCost at sizes that depend on the rounded length), not as one closed polynomial.

Permit witnesses (the ten-token audit SKY-5, closed by part close-f for the ECRECOVER way of permit(address,address,uint256,uint256,uint8,bytes32,bytes32)): Instance.permit_runs (Sky/PermitRun.lean) is one machine-checked successful run: permit(SIGNER, SIGNER, 1000, 2^256 - 1, 27, r, s) sent by CALLER1, chain id 1, any address C, all-zero storage, 100000 gas, under the real runner of EthLib (the precompile ECRECOVER is run by the kernel on a real secp256k1 signature, nothing about it is assumed), Paris <= fork < Glamsterdam: it ends with no error, the allowance is 1000 and the nonce of SIGNER is 1. Instance.permit_runs_inv: the same run ends in a state where Inv holds, under Sep (callKeys m1) (not proved). The state hypothesis NoDelegation1 is discharged for concrete states (Instance.noDelegation1_sState and two more). Still NOT covered: (1) no successful run of the ERC-1271 way (a contract owner that answers isValidSignature): it needs a concrete owner contract and a forward rule for a STATICCALL to code; (2) no successful run of permit(address,address,uint256,uint256,bytes) (the bytes entry), by ECRECOVER or by ERC-1271; (3) no run of the permit path where the chain id differs from the one at deployment (DOMAIN_SEPARATOR rebuilt). For these paths the completeness theorems are sound but not shown non-empty. Every other success path has a witness.

ERC-1271 route: the gas left after the call is an inequality; the state the callee starts from is given through the caller frame EthLib builds, not as a closed formula; the return size is stated as a word.

Sequence theorems of the older model (Seq.lean, PermitSeq.lean, PermitBytesSeq.lean) still assume that the steps that are not top-level calls to the token keep its storage; the transaction theorems of Sky/Tx.lean replace them (the ten-token audit SKY-3, closed in the fix round of the ONDO audit). Sep is assumed, not proved, and cannot be proved in Lean; for one concrete call it is reduced to the 5 facts Instance.KeyFacts (the ten-token audit SKY-4, closed as far as Lean can go).
Transaction level: what a block does between transactions is not linked (withdrawals, the system calls of EIP-4788, 2935, 7002, 7251, rewards). Seq.Chain strings transactions only.

Transaction level: forks before Dencun. There the end of a transaction can delete an account that ran SELFDESTRUCT, and it is not proved here that the code of SKY never runs it (the library tracks instead that C is not created in the transaction and not marked for deletion, which EIP-6780 gives from Dencun).
Transaction level: Glamsterdam and later (two-counter gas meter).
Transaction level: the base case of supply_from_zero is all-zero storage; the constructor run that leaves the real start state is not linked, so nothing is proved about the real chain state.
Transaction level: NoDelegation1 at each entry into the token is assumed, not derived from a start state (no theorem that a run keeps address 1 free of delegation code).

No theorem over sequences of calls for wards: 'wards change only by rely and deny' and 'only a ward mints' are facts of one call each (see contract_findings). A sequence form needs, per function, that the slot of wards[a] is kept, which needs keccak separation of the wards slots from the balance, allowance and nonce slots (Sep states it only for the keys of one call). So every claim about wards in this file is worded per call (the ten-token audit SKY-6): no sequence form was added, because the kit library TokenKit/Seq carries state predicates that read the storage of the token only (Seq.StorageOnly), and "wards changes only by rely and deny" is a relation between two states under a keccak hypothesis for every address, not such a predicate.
Sanity witnesses for name(), symbol(), version() (read-only loops: ro_ theorems only, as for USDD and DAI).
Only completeness (a successful run implies the facts); the converse is the Sanity witnesses, per path, not in general.
Unchecked sums are stated as 256-bit words in Readable.lean; the exact natural-number forms need the invariant (Sky/Exact.lean).
From Glamsterdam on (two-counter gas meter): nothing. See fork_range.
Verified Solidity source not compared; all statements are about the deployed bytes.
contract_findings: Per call (mint_readable), not a theorem over sequences: a mint(to, value) call that succeeds was sent by an address with wards[caller] = 1 at the start of that call; no cap other than totalSupply not overflowing; to must not be 0 or the contract.

Per call (rely_readable, deny_readable), not a theorem over sequences: a rely(usr) or deny(usr) call that succeeds was sent by an address with wards[caller] = 1 at the start of that call, writes the one slot wards[usr] (1 or 0) and logs Rely / Deny (two topics, no data); a ward can deny itself or any other ward. That no other function writes a wards slot is read from the per-function readable theorems under Sep (each lists the slots it writes); it is not proved as one theorem, and there is no theorem 'wards change only by rely and deny' over a sequence of calls.
burn(from, value) needs no ward: the holder, or a spender with allowance (the largest allowance is not reduced).
transfer and transferFrom reject to = 0 and to = the contract; address arguments with dirty high bits revert (0.8 ABI decoder).
The additions to a balance and the subtraction from totalSupply in burn are unchecked in the code; they cannot wrap while sum of balances = totalSupply (proved).
permit increments the nonce BEFORE the outside call; the outside call is a STATICCALL, so the owner's code cannot re-enter a writer.
DOMAIN_SEPARATOR(): a constant when the chain id is 1, computed from the chain id and the contract address otherwise; deploymentChainId() returns 1.
No value is accepted by any function; no selfdestruct, no delegatecall, no upgrade hook in the bytes.

reuse_notes: Outside calls (LINK transferAndCall, WBTC, CRO): TokenKit.staticcall_kept is general for STATICCALL only. For CALL the callee may write and log: use TokenKit/Evm/CallOutcome.lean (call_outcome, Sent) and state what the callee may change; a KeepsOn-style assumption is then needed for the token's own storage unless the token cannot be re-entered.

Pattern that worked: stops at the GAS before the call, generated prefix and segments with raw_mem, a RunsTo relation (gas bound, not exact gas) across the call (TokenKit/Evm/Tail.lean), joins hand-written per memory layout.
